answer: At a wharf, agents buying pigment pay couriers with signed cumulative payment-channel vouchers as deliveries pulse through the dock. Each voucher binds a channel ID, recipient and total owed. Settlement pays only the increase over that channel's previously redeemed total, never the full voucher again. Relaying old vouchers through a thousand aliases cannot multiply payment; the channel balance caps liability. This blocks sybil redemption farming, assuming secure signatures and atomic settlement.
